assets.title: Moscow & Kremlin Skyline
assets.details: High aerial view over the Moskva River, capturing the historic red-brick towers of the Moscow Kremlin, Cathedral of Christ the Saviour, and golden cathedral domes.

assets.title: Crimean Mountain Peaks
assets.details: Spectacular flight over the limestone precipices and karst plateaus of the Crimean Mountains rising dramatically above the azure waters of the Black Sea.

assets.title: Russian Taiga & Northern Forest I
assets.details: Endless pristine canopy of the Siberian taiga, the world's largest forested wilderness, stretching uninterrupted across vast boreal river basins.

assets.title: Russian Taiga & Wilderness II
assets.details: Vast Siberian wilderness of evergreen taiga and pristine winding rivers, capturing the untouched boreal expanse of northern Eurasia.

assets.title: Russian Taiga River & Forest III
assets.details: Sweeping flight over Siberian boreal riverbanks and ancient pine forests stretching toward the Arctic horizon.

assets.title: Russian Birch & Boreal Forest
assets.details: Sunlit flight above vibrant white birch groves and evergreen pine forests in rural Russia during peak seasonal autumn foliage.

assets.title: Rila Monastery
assets.details: Founded in the 10th century by Saint John of Rila, this Eastern Orthodox monastery sits at 1,147 m in the forested Rila Mountains. Renowned for its distinctive striped colonnades, intricate vibrant frescoes, and the 14th-century stone Tower of Hrelyo, it stands as Bulgaria's cultural and spiritual sanctuary.

assets.title: Seven Rila Lakes
assets.details: A group of glacial lakes situated in the northwestern Rila Mountains between 2,100 and 2,500 meters altitude. Cascading into each other from the highest 'The Tear' to 'The Eye', 'The Kidney', 'The Twin', 'The Trefoil', 'Fish Lake', and 'The Lower Lake', they form Bulgaria's most visited alpine wonderland.

assets.title: Belogradchik Rocks and Fortress
assets.details: A striking formation of reddish and yellowish sandstone and conglomerate rock pinnacles sculpted over 200 million years, reaching up to 200 meters high on the western slopes of the Balkan Mountains. Built naturally into the towers is the ancient Belogradchik Fortress, dating back to Roman times.

assets.title: Ancient City of Nessebar
assets.details: An ancient Black Sea peninsula with over 3,000 years of civilization, known as the 'Pearl of the Black Sea'. Connected to the mainland by a narrow isthmus with a wooden windmill, this UNESCO World Heritage town showcases remarkable medieval churches, timber houses, and seaside fortifications.

assets.title: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, Sofia
assets.details: One of the largest Eastern Orthodox cathedrals in the world, built in Neo-Byzantine style with gold-plated and copper domes soaring 53 meters high. Serving as the primary cathedral of the Bulgarian Patriarchate, it dominates the historic heart of Sofia.

assets.title: Buzludzha Monument
assets.details: Perched atop Mount Buzludzha at 1,441 m along the Central Balkan Mountains ridge, this colossal saucer-shaped brutalist structure and 70-meter tower was opened in 1981. Now an enigmatic world-renowned relic of 20th-century history, it stands amid sweeping panoramic mountain vistas.

assets.title: Old Town & Roman Theatre, Plovdiv
assets.details: Continuously inhabited for over 8,000 years, Plovdiv is one of the oldest cities in Europe. Its historic Old Town spreads across three granite hills (Nebet Tepe), featuring ornate National Revival mansions and a remarkably preserved 1st-century Roman amphitheatre overlooking the city.

photos.title: Christ the Redeemer — Paul Landowski, 1931, Corcovado, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
photos.description: Colossal Art Deco statue of Jesus Christ created by French sculptor Paul Landowski and Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa. Standing 30 meters tall atop the 700-meter Corcovado peak overlooking Rio de Janeiro, it was constructed between 1922 and 1931 from reinforced concrete and six million soapstone tiles. In 2007, it was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

photos.title: David — Michelangelo, 1504, Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence, Italy
photos.description: Masterpiece of Renaissance sculpture created in pure Carrara marble by Michelangelo between 1501 and 1504. Standing 5.17 meters tall, the statue portrays the biblical hero David, poised with intense focus before facing Goliath. Its anatomical accuracy and contrapposto stance established it as the supreme symbol of Florentine civic liberty.

photos.title: Mask of Tutankhamun — 18th Dynasty Gold Mask, c. 1323 BC, Luxor / Cairo, Egypt
photos.description: Ancient Egyptian gold funerary mask of the 18th Dynasty pharaoh Tutankhamun, crafted around 1323 BC. Discovered in 1925 in the Valley of the Kings by Howard Carter, it is fashioned from two sheets of beaten high-karat gold inlaid with colored glass, faience, and semi-precious lapis lazuli.

photos.title: Great Sphinx of Giza — Old Kingdom Colossal Sculpture, c. 2500 BC, Giza, Egypt
photos.description: Colossal limestone statue of a reclining mythical sphinx with the body of a lion and the head of Pharaoh Khafre, carved around 2500 BC during Egypt's Old Kingdom. Measuring 73 meters long and 20 meters high, it is the oldest known monumental sculpture in Egypt.

photos.title: Benin Bronzes — Kingdom of Benin Royal Sculptures, 16th c., Benin City, Nigeria
photos.description: Group of over a thousand commemorative brass and bronze plaques and cast sculptures created by the Edo people of the Kingdom of Benin from the 16th century onward. Adorning the royal palace of the Oba, their intricate lost-wax casting exemplifies West African metalworking mastery.

photos.title: Church of St. George — Rock-Hewn Monolithic Church, c. 1200, Lalibela, Ethiopia
photos.description: Monolithic cross-shaped church carved directly downward into volcanic tuff rock during the late 12th or early 13th century under King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela. Connected by a subterranean network of trenches and catacombs, it remains an active pilgrimage site of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.

photos.title: Great Mosque of Djenné — Sudano-Sahelian Earth Architecture, c. 13th c., Djenné, Mali
photos.description: The largest mud-brick architecture in the world, situated along the Bani River in Mali. Built in the distinctive Sudano-Sahelian architectural style with sun-baked earth bricks, its walls are replastered annually by the entire community during an extraordinary cultural festival.

photos.title: Ife Head of a King — Kingdom of Ife Brass Sculpture, c. 1300, Ife, Nigeria
photos.description: Masterpiece of Yoruba naturalistic sculpture cast in copper alloy around 1300 AD in the ancient sacred city of Ile-Ife. Unearthed in 1938, its refined facial features and delicate striations represent an Ooni (king) wearing a beaded royal headdress.

photos.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa — Hokusai, c. 1831, Mount Fuji, Japan
photos.description: Famous woodblock print by the Japanese ukiyo-e master Katsushika Hokusai, published around 1831 as the first print in Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji. Depicts towering rogue waves framing Japan's sacred Mount Fuji, with three oared cargo boats bravely navigating the turbulent seas.

photos.title: Along the River During the Qingming Festival — Zhang Zeduan, Song Dynasty, Bianjing, China
photos.description: Panoramic Song Dynasty handscroll painting by Zhang Zeduan from the early 12th century, capturing the vibrant daily life, commerce, and celebrations in the imperial capital of Bianjing (modern Kaifeng) along the Yellow River during the annual Qingming festival.

photos.title: Terracotta Army — Qin Dynasty Sculptures, c. 210 BC, Xi'an, China
photos.description: Monumental funerary collection of more than 8,000 life-sized terracotta soldiers, 130 chariots, and 520 horses buried around 210 BC to protect Qin Shi Huang, the first Emperor of China, in the afterlife. Every single soldier displays unique facial features, armor, and hairstyles.

photos.title: Taj Mahal — Mughal Monumental Architecture, 1648, Agra, India
photos.description: Ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna River, commissioned in 1631 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal. Celebrated as the jewel of Muslim art in India, it features symmetry, Persian calligraphy, and pietra dura inlays.

photos.title: Padmapani Bodhisattva Fresco — Ajanta Caves, c. 475 AD, Maharashtra, India
photos.description: Ancient Buddhist cave fresco painted around 475 AD inside Cave 1 of the Ajanta Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage site in the Sahyadri mountains. Depicts Bodhisattva Padmapani holding a blue lotus flower, radiating compassion with subtle shading and spiritual elegance.

photos.title: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple — Chandela Dynasty, c. 1030 AD, Khajuraho, India
photos.description: The largest and most ornate Hindu temple at Khajuraho, built around 1030 AD by the Chandela king Vidyadhara. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, its towering spire represents Mount Meru, adorned with over 800 intricately carved sculptures celebrating divine joy and artistic perfection.

photos.title: Angkor Wat — Khmer Monumental Architecture, c. 1150 AD, Siem Reap, Cambodia
photos.description: Massive temple complex constructed in the early 12th century by Khmer King Suryavarman II, originally dedicated to Vishnu before transforming into a Buddhist center. Spanning over 160 hectares, it is the largest religious monument in the world, surrounded by a vast moat.

photos.title: Borobudur Temple Stupas — Sailendra Dynasty, c. 800 AD, Java, Indonesia
photos.description: The world's largest Buddhist temple, built in the 8th and 9th centuries under the Sailendra Dynasty. Constructed without mortar from volcanic rock, its concentric terraces ascend past 2,672 relief panels and 504 Buddha statues toward a central monumental dome.

photos.title: Gate of All Nations — Achaemenid Empire, c. 515 BC, Persepolis, Iran
photos.description: Grand entrance portal ordered by King Xerxes I around 515 BC at Persepolis, the ceremonial capital of the Persian Achaemenid Empire. Guarded by colossal winged human-headed bulls (lamassu), it welcomed envoys and dignitaries from all provinces of the vast empire.

photos.title: El Castillo (Pyramid of Kukulkan) — Maya Civilization, c. 900 AD, Chichen Itza, Mexico
photos.description: Mesoamerican step-pyramid dedicated to the feathered serpent deity Kukulkan, built by the Maya civilization between the 9th and 12th centuries. During the equinoxes, the afternoon sun casts shadows creating the illusion of a giant serpent slithering down the stairs.

photos.title: Pyramid of the Sun — Pre-Columbian City, c. 200 AD, Teotihuacan, Mexico
photos.description: The largest structure in the ancient pre-Columbian city of Teotihuacan, built around 200 AD along the Avenue of the Dead. Rising 65 meters above the valley floor, it served as an astronomical observatory and ceremonial temple dedicated to celestial deities.

photos.title: Aztec Sun Stone (Piedra del Sol) — Aztec Empire, c. 1502, Tenochtitlan / Mexico City
photos.description: Colossal basalt calendar monolith carved in the early 16th century by the Mexica (Aztec) Empire under Emperor Moctezuma II. Unearthed beneath Mexico City's Zócalo in 1790, it depicts the central face of the sun god Tonatiuh surrounded by four previous cosmic eras.

photos.title: Machu Picchu Sanctuary — Inca Empire, c. 1450, Andes Mountains, Cusco, Peru
photos.description: Inca royal citadel situated on a mountain ridge 2,430 meters above sea level in the Sacred Valley of Peru, constructed around 1450 under Emperor Pachacuti. Known for its sophisticated dry-stone masonry, agricultural terraces, and dramatic alpine panorama.

photos.title: Moai of Rapa Nui — Polynesian Monolithic Statues, c. 1250–1500, Easter Island, Chile
photos.description: Monolithic volcanic stone figures carved by the Polynesian Rapa Nui people between 1250 and 1500 AD. Representing ancestral chiefs, nearly 1,000 statues stand across the remote Pacific island, gazing inland from monumental stone platforms called ahu.

photos.title: American Gothic — Grant Wood, 1930, Eldon, Iowa / Art Institute of Chicago
photos.description: Iconic 1930 regionalist painting by Grant Wood, inspired by the Carpenter Gothic house in Eldon, Iowa. Depicting a farmer holding a pitchfork alongside his daughter, it captures the stoic spirit and work ethic of small-town rural America during the Great Depression.

photos.title: Nighthawks — Edward Hopper, 1942, New York / Art Institute of Chicago
photos.description: Atmospheric 1942 oil painting by Edward Hopper portraying four late-night patrons seated in an illuminated downtown diner on a quiet city corner. Renowned for its subtle depiction of urban solitude, cinematic lighting, and modernist architectural geometry.

photos.title: Aboriginal Rock Art — Indigenous Australian Ancestral Art, Kakadu, Australia
photos.description: Ancient Indigenous Australian rock art gallery in Kakadu National Park, Northern Territory, dating back over 20,000 years. Painted by Bininj/Mungguy artists using natural ochre pigments, it documents ancestral creation stories, native wildlife, and the spiritual Rainbow Serpent.

photos.title: Mona Lisa — Leonardo da Vinci, c. 1503, Musée du Louvre, Paris, France
photos.description: Celebrated Renaissance portrait painted in oil on poplar wood by Leonardo da Vinci, begun around 1503 in Florence. Famous for its subtle sfumato blending, enigmatic smile, and imaginary mountainous landscape, it is the most visited painting in the Musée du Louvre.

photos.title: The Starry Night — Vincent van Gogh, 1889, Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, France
photos.description: Post-impressionist masterpiece painted by Vincent van Gogh in June 1889 from his asylum room window at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. Features swirling celestial rhythms, glowing crescents and stars, and an expressive foreground cypress tree.

photos.title: The Birth of Venus — Sandro Botticelli, c. 1485, Uffizi Gallery, Florence, Italy
photos.description: Renaissance canvas painted around 1485 by Sandro Botticelli, depicting the goddess Venus emerging from the sea upon a scallop shell, blown ashore by the winds Zephyr and Aura. Preserved in Florence's Uffizi Gallery, it embodies Neoplatonic humanist ideals.

photos.title: The Creation of Adam — Michelangelo, 1512, Sistine Chapel, Vatican City
photos.description: Monumental fresco painted by Michelangelo between 1508 and 1512 upon the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel. Illustrating the biblical creation narrative from Genesis, the nearly touching fingertips of God and Adam form one of the most celebrated gestures in Western art.

photos.title: The Thinker — Auguste Rodin, 1904, Musée Rodin, Paris, France
photos.description: Iconic bronze sculpture created by French sculptor Auguste Rodin, conceived in 1880 as part of The Gates of Hell inspired by Dante's Inferno. Depicts a muscular male figure leaning forward in deep philosophical meditation, symbolizing human contemplation and creative struggle.

photos.title: The Kiss — Gustav Klimt, 1908, Belvedere Palace, Vienna, Austria
photos.description: Sensual Golden Phase painting by Austrian symbolist Gustav Klimt, completed in 1908. Using gold leaf, silver, and intricate geometric patterns, it portrays two lovers wrapped in an ornate embrace atop a bed of wild alpine blossoms in Vienna's Belvedere Palace.

photos.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring — Johannes Vermeer, 1665, Mauritshuis, The Hague
photos.description: Exquisite Dutch Golden Age tronie painted around 1665 by Johannes Vermeer. Renowned for its luminous rendering of light, exotic blue turban, and reflective teardrop pearl, it captivates viewers with her momentary over-the-shoulder glance.

photos.title: The Night Watch — Rembrandt, 1642, Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, Netherlands
photos.description: Monumental 1642 masterpiece by Rembrandt van Rijn, depicting Captain Frans Banninck Cocq and his civic militia company preparing to march. Acclaimed for its dramatic chiaroscuro lighting, dynamic motion, and life-size group composition in the Rijksmuseum.

photos.title: Venus de Milo — Alexandros of Antioch, c. 150 BC, Milos, Greece
photos.description: Classical Hellenistic marble sculpture carved around 150 BC on the Aegean island of Milos, attributed to Alexandros of Antioch. Standing over 2 meters tall, the graceful goddess of love and beauty is renowned worldwide for her classic S-curve contrapposto.

photos.title: Winged Victory of Samothrace — Hellenistic Sculpture, c. 190 BC, Samothrace, Greece
photos.description: Monumental Parian marble sculpture of the goddess Nike, created around 190 BC on the Greek island of Samothrace to celebrate a naval triumph. Perched upon a ship's prow with rippling drapery swept by sea winds, it presides over the Daru staircase in the Louvre.

photos.title: The Colosseum — Flavian Amphitheatre, 80 AD, Rome, Italy
photos.description: The largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, constructed in limestone, tuff, and brick-faced concrete under the Flavian emperors between 72 and 80 AD. Seating over 50,000 spectators for gladiatorial contests, it remains the ultimate architectural icon of Imperial Rome.

photos.title: The Parthenon & Acropolis — Classical Greek Architecture, c. 447 BC, Athens, Greece
photos.description: Former temple dedicated to the goddess Athena, constructed between 447 and 432 BC atop the rocky Acropolis of Athens by architects Ictinus and Callicrates under Pericles. Regarded as the zenith of Doric classical architecture and Western democratic heritage.

photos.title: The Scream — Edvard Munch, 1893, National Museum, Oslo, Norway
photos.description: Pioneering expressionist composition created in 1893 by Norwegian artist Edvard Munch. Depicting an agonized figure under an infernal orange sunset along the Kristiania fjord, it externalizes Munch's sensation of an infinite, piercing scream passing through nature.

photos.title: Las Meninas — Diego Velázquez, 1656, Museo del Prado, Madrid, Spain
photos.description: Complex Golden Age painting created in 1656 by Diego Velázquez in the Royal Alcázar of Madrid. Depicting the young Infanta Margaret Theresa attended by her retinue, with Velázquez himself at the easel and the King and Queen reflected in a rear mirror.

photos.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog — Caspar David Friedrich, 1818, Dresden / Hamburg
photos.description: Romantic oil painting by Caspar David Friedrich, completed in 1818. Depicting a lone traveler standing upon a rocky precipice gazing out over a sweeping landscape cloaked in mountain fog, it epitomizes the Romantic encounter with the sublime in nature.

photos.title: Madara Rider — Early Medieval Rock Relief, c. 710 AD, Madara, Bulgaria
photos.description: Early medieval monumental rock relief carved around 710 AD into a vertical 100-meter cliff near Madara in northeastern Bulgaria. Depicting a horseman triumphant over a lion, followed by a hunting dog, it is a UNESCO World Heritage site honoring the early Bulgarian rulers.

photos.title: Boyana Church Frescoes — Medieval Master, 1259, Boyana, Sofia, Bulgaria
photos.description: Medieval Bulgarian Orthodox church located at the foot of Mount Vitosha in Sofia. Its exceptional 1259 frescoes by a master Bulgarian iconographer display remarkable psychological depth, realism, and vibrant color, foreshadowing the European Renaissance by decades.

photos.title: Rila Monastery Frescoes — Zahari Zograf, c. 1844, Rila, Bulgaria
photos.description: The spiritual and cultural heart of Bulgaria, founded in the 10th century in the Rila Mountains. Its 1844 exterior frescoes by Zahari Zograf feature brilliant biblical scenes, angels, and virtues, representing the pinnacle of the Bulgarian National Revival.

photos.title: The Bronze Horseman — Étienne Falconet, 1782, Senate Square, Saint Petersburg, Russia
photos.description: Monumental equestrian statue of Peter the Great, commissioned by Catherine the Great and sculpted by Étienne Maurice Falconet between 1768 and 1782 on the bank of the Neva River. Peter points westward atop the Thunder Stone, the largest stone ever moved by humans.

photos.title: Morning in a Pine Forest — Ivan Shishkin, 1889, Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow, Russia
photos.description: Beloved 1889 Russian landscape painting by Ivan Shishkin, featuring four brown bear cubs playing among fallen trees in a misty primordial forest. Renowned for Shishkin's masterly depiction of morning sunlight filtering through ancient pine crowns.

photos.title: The Ninth Wave — Ivan Aivazovsky, 1850, State Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg, Russia
photos.description: Epic 1850 marine masterpiece by Russian romantic painter Ivan Aivazovsky. Depicting castaways clinging to a broken mast after a nocturnal storm as the luminous morning sun breaks through crashing ocean swells, it symbolizes hope amidst the raw power of the sea.

photos.title: Barge Haulers on the Volga — Ilya Repin, 1873, State Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg, Russia
photos.description: Seminal 1873 realist oil painting by Ilya Repin, depicting eleven exhausted burlaks (barge haulers) straining against heavy leather straps to pull a barge up the Volga River under the blazing sun. Praised by Tolstoy, it is an enduring tribute to human dignity.

photos.title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji) — Hokusai, c. 1831, Edo / Mount Fuji, Japan
photos.description: Iconic woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji' series. Depicts Mount Fuji bathed in reddish morning sunlight in late summer, with delicate white mackerel clouds drifting across an intense Prussian blue sky.

photos.title: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge — Utagawa Hiroshige, 1857, Edo / Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Masterpiece woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige from 'One Hundred Famous Views of Edo' (1857). Shows pedestrians scrambling across the Great Bridge over the Sumida River during a violent summer cloudburst, famously admired and copied in oil by Vincent van Gogh.

photos.title: Plum Park in Kameido — Utagawa Hiroshige, 1857, Edo / Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Celebrated woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige (1857) featuring the famous 'Sleeping Dragon Plum' tree (Garyūbai). The composition uses a bold, close-up foreground framing device that deeply influenced Western Post-Impressionism.

photos.title: Red and White Plum Blossoms — Ogata Kōrin, c. 1716, MOA Museum of Art, Atami, Japan
photos.description: National Treasure pair of two-panel folding screens by Ogata Kōrin (c. 1716), master of the Rinpa school. Features swirling metallic silver river waters flanked by stylized blooming plum trees, blending abstract graphic design with profound naturalism.

photos.title: Irises Screen — Ogata Kōrin, c. 1701, Nezu Museum, Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: National Treasure pair of six-panel folding screens by Ogata Kōrin (c. 1701), painted with precious azurite and malachite pigments on gold leaf. Illustrates an episode from the 10th-century 'Tales of Ise' at the Eight Bridges of Mikawa province.

photos.title: Cypress Trees Screen — Kanō Eitoku, 1590, Tokyo National Museum, Japan
photos.description: National Treasure eight-panel folding screen by Azuchi-Momoyama master Kanō Eitoku (1590). Executed in color and gold leaf on paper, it portrays a colossal, gnarled ancient cypress tree symbolizing enduring power and majesty.

photos.title: Otani Oniji III as Edobei — Tōshūsai Sharaku, 1794, Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Famous Edo-period kabuki portrait print by the enigmatic master Tōshūsai Sharaku (1794). Depicts actor Otani Oniji III as the villainous servant Yakko Edobei with tensed hands, wild eyes, and open mouth, capturing an intense dramatic climax.

photos.title: Three Beauties of the Present Day — Kitagawa Utamaro, c. 1793, Edo / Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Masterpiece ukiyo-e print by Kitagawa Utamaro (c. 1793) depicting three celebrated beauties of 1790s Edo: geisha Tomimoto Toyohina, and teahouse waitresses Naniwa Kita and Takashima Hisa, set against a sparkling mica-dusted background.

photos.title: Pine Trees in the Snow — Maruyama Ōkyo, 1780s, Mitsui Memorial Museum, Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Pair of six-panel folding screens by Maruyama Ōkyo (1780s), designated a National Treasure of Japan. Executed in ink and light color with gold dust, it captures heavy snow resting on evergreen pine boughs using reserve white paper technique.

photos.title: Landscape in Splashed Ink (Haboku Sansui) — Sesshū Tōyō, 1495, Tokyo National Museum, Japan
photos.description: National Treasure hanging scroll by Zen Buddhist monk and master Sesshū Tōyō (1495). Created using the spontaneous 'splashed ink' (haboku) technique, expressing towering misty mountains and a solitary boatman with rapid, calligraphic brushstrokes.

photos.title: Travelers Among Mountains and Streams — Fan Kuan, c. 1000, National Palace Museum, Taipei
photos.description: Monumental Northern Song hanging scroll by Fan Kuan (c. 1000), widely regarded as the pinnacle of Chinese landscape painting. Towering granite cliffs rise above mist-shrouded valleys where a tiny pack mule caravan winds along a rocky path.

photos.title: Early Spring — Guo Xi, 1072, Northern Song Dynasty, National Palace Museum, Taipei
photos.description: National Treasure Northern Song hanging scroll by Guo Xi (1072). Demonstrates the 'three distances' perspective, capturing the awakening of nature after winter with vaporous mists, surging mountain ridges, and gnarled pine trees.

photos.title: On a Mountain Path in Spring — Ma Yuan, c. 1200, Southern Song Dynasty, National Palace Museum
photos.description: Exquisite Southern Song album leaf by Ma Yuan (c. 1200), known as 'One-Corner Ma' for his evocative asymmetric compositions. A scholar accompanied by a servant walks along a willow path while watching a singing oriole.

photos.title: Emperor Qianlong in Ceremonial Armor — Giuseppe Castiglione (Lang Shining), 1739, Beijing, China
photos.description: Monumental hanging scroll by Jesuit court painter Giuseppe Castiglione (Lang Shining, 1739). Depicts the Qing Dynasty Qianlong Emperor on horseback in full ceremonial gold armor, synthesizing European oil realism with Chinese ink tradition.

photos.title: Court Ladies of Former Shu — Tang Yin, c. 1520, Palace Museum, Beijing, China
photos.description: Renowned Ming Dynasty hanging scroll by Tang Yin (Tang Bohu, c. 1520), one of the Four Masters of Ming. Portrays four elegant imperial palace ladies in opulent Five Dynasties attire, painted with refined gongbi brushwork.

photos.title: Poet on a Mountaintop — Shen Zhou, c. 1490, Ming Dynasty, Nelson-Atkins Museum
photos.description: Celebrated Ming Dynasty album leaf by Shen Zhou (c. 1490), founder of the Wu School of literati painting. A solitary poet stands atop a windswept plateau gazing across rolling mist, accompanied by a self-inscribed poem on the harmony of mind and landscape.

photos.title: Autumn Colors on the Qiao and Hua Mountains — Zhao Mengfu, 1295, Yuan Dynasty
photos.description: Handscroll by Yuan Dynasty master Zhao Mengfu (1295), painted for his friend Zhou Mi. Depicts the distinctive rounded Mount Hua and cone-shaped Mount Qiao in Shandong province, ushering in the scholar-amateur literati style.

photos.title: Immortal in Splashed Ink — Liang Kai, c. 1200, National Palace Museum, Taipei
photos.description: Masterpiece album leaf by Southern Song painter Liang Kai (c. 1200). Rendered with miraculous economy of wet, abbreviated brushwork, capturing the eccentric, laughing spirit of a Chan Buddhist immortal in a few swift strokes.

photos.title: Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains — Huang Gongwang, 1350, Yuan Dynasty
photos.description: Legendary Yuan Dynasty handscroll by Huang Gongwang (1350), one of the Four Masters of the Yuan. Painted over three years along the scenic Fuchun River in Zhejiang, revered as a supreme masterpiece of Chinese literati landscape art.

photos.title: Shakuntala Looking Back for Dushyanta — Raja Ravi Varma, 1898, Kerala / Bangalore, India
photos.description: Celebrated 1898 oil painting by Raja Ravi Varma depicting heroine Shakuntala from the Mahabharata pretending to remove a thorn from her foot while turning back to catch a secret glimpse of King Dushyanta in the forest.

photos.title: Damayanti Talking to the Swan — Raja Ravi Varma, c. 1899, Trivandrum, India
photos.description: Masterpiece oil painting by Raja Ravi Varma (c. 1899) illustrating the tale of Nala and Damayanti from the Mahabharata. Princess Damayanti listens intently as a celestial golden swan sings the praises of King Nala.

photos.title: Radha of Kishangarh (Bani Thani) — Nihâl Chand, c. 1750, National Museum, New Delhi, India
photos.description: Iconic 18th-century Rajput miniature by court painter Nihâl Chand (c. 1750), often called the 'Mona Lisa of India'. Depicts the singer and poet Bani Thani as the Hindu goddess Radha, with exaggerated lotus eyes, arched eyebrows, and sheer gold-bordered veil.

photos.title: Jahangir Preferring a Sufi Shaikh to Kings — Bichitr, c. 1620, Mughal Empire, Agra, India
photos.description: Intricate Mughal miniature from the St. Petersburg Album by court artist Bichitr (c. 1620). Depicts Emperor Jahangir seated on an hourglass throne presenting a book to a venerable Sufi mystic while European King James I and Ottoman Sultan look on.

photos.title: Krishna and Radha in a Pavilion — Pahari / Kangra School, c. 1780, Himachal Pradesh, India
photos.description: Exquisite Pahari miniature from the Kangra School (c. 1780) illustrating Jayadeva's Gita Govinda. The divine lovers Krishna and Radha embrace in an ornate marble pavilion under a dark monsoon sky illuminated by a streak of golden lightning.

photos.title: Galaxy of Musicians — Raja Ravi Varma, 1889, Mysore Palace, Karnataka, India
photos.description: Monumental 1889 oil canvas by Raja Ravi Varma painted for the Maharaja of Mysore. Depicts eleven Indian women in diverse regional traditional attire playing indigenous musical instruments, celebrating the unified cultural tapestry of India.

photos.title: Bride's Toilet — Amrita Sher-Gil, 1937, National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi, India
photos.description: Seminal 1937 modern oil painting by pioneer Indian modernist Amrita Sher-Gil. Depicts a young Indian bride dressed in luminous saffron surrounded by her family members, blending European post-impressionism with classical Ajanta cave fresco aesthetics.

photos.title: Shiva Nataraja (Lord of the Dance) — Chola Dynasty Bronze, 11th c., Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India
photos.description: 11th-century lost-wax bronze masterpiece of the Chola Dynasty from Tamil Nadu. Depicts the cosmic dance (Ananda Tandava) of Shiva within an aureole of flames, embodying the continuous cycle of creation, preservation, and destruction of the universe.

photos.title: The Court of Gayumars — Sultan Muhammad, c. 1522, Shahnameh of Shah Tahmasp, Tabriz, Iran
photos.description: Supreme masterpiece of Persian miniature painting from the Shahnameh of Shah Tahmasp, painted by Sultan Muhammad (c. 1522). Depicts King Gayumars enthroned atop a miraculous flowering mountain among court nobles clad in leopard skins.

photos.title: The Seduction of Yusuf (Joseph fleeing Zulaikha) — Kamāl ud-Dīn Behzād, 1488, Herat / Cairo
photos.description: Famous Persian miniature by Kamāl ud-Dīn Behzād (1488) illustrating Jami's Haft Awrang. Portrays Yusuf fleeing through seven locked rooms of an intricate labyrinthine palace designed by Zulaikha, celebrated for its brilliant architectural perspective.

photos.title: Two Lovers — Reza Abbasi, 1630, Safavid Empire, Isfahan, Iran
photos.description: Exquisite Safavid miniature painting by court master Reza Abbasi (1630) in Isfahan. Depicts two youthful lovers in an intimate embrace wrapped in rich Persian textiles, capturing the sensual elegance of 17th-century Isfahani courtly culture.

photos.title: Surname-i Vehbi Imperial Festival — Abdülcelil Levni, c. 1720, Topkapi Palace, Istanbul, Turkey
photos.description: Ottoman miniature by court painter Abdülcelil Levni (c. 1720) illustrating the imperial circumcision festival of Sultan Ahmed III. Depicts guild artisans and acrobats parading across the Hippodrome in Constantinople with lavish floats.

photos.title: Striding Lion Glazed Relief — Processional Way of Babylon, c. 575 BC, Mesopotamia / Iraq
photos.description: Neo-Babylonian glazed polychrome brick relief from the Processional Way of Babylon (c. 575 BC) during the reign of Nebuchadnezzar II. The sacred lion of the goddess Ishtar strided along the sacred ceremonial avenue to the Ishtar Gate.

photos.title: The Royal Lion Hunt of Ashurbanipal — Neo-Assyrian Relief, c. 645 BC, Nineveh / Mosul, Iraq
photos.description: Triumphant alabaster bas-relief from the North Palace of Nineveh (c. 645 BC). Depicts the great Assyrian king Ashurbanipal in his chariot hunting desert lions, celebrated worldwide for the intense muscular realism and pathos of the wounded animals.

photos.title: Achaemenid Immortals Glazed Frieze — Palace of Darius, c. 510 BC, Susa, Iran
photos.description: Glazed siliceous brick frieze from the Apadana Palace of Darius the Great at Susa (c. 510 BC). Depicts the elite elite Persian royal guard known as 'The Immortals', adorned in embroidered robes and armed with spears, bows, and quivers.

photos.title: Complete View of Mount Geumgang (Geumgangjeondo) — Jeong Seon, 1734, Joseon Dynasty, Korea
photos.description: National Treasure of Korea painted by Joseon master Jeong Seon (1734). Pioneered the True-View Landscape (Jingyeong Sansuwha) movement, capturing the sacred 12,000 serrated granite peaks of the Diamond Mountains with dynamic rhythmic brushwork.

photos.title: Ssireum (Korean Wrestling) — Kim Hong-do (Danwon), c. 1780, Joseon Dynasty, Seoul, Korea
photos.description: Iconic Joseon genre painting by Kim Hong-do (Danwon, c. 1780) from the Danwon Pungsokdo Album. Captures two wrestlers locked in a tense throw surrounded by a circular audience of animated spectators reacting with suspense and humor.

photos.title: The Flower Carrier (Cargador de Flores) — Diego Rivera, 1935, Mexico City, Mexico
photos.description: Celebrated 1935 oil and tempera painting by Mexican master Diego Rivera. Portrays an indigenous peasant on hands and knees struggling under an enormous basket of colorful pink flowers, symbolizing the heavy burdens of the working class.

photos.title: Portrait of Frida Kahlo in Studio — Guillermo Kahlo, 1932, Coyoacán, Mexico City, Mexico
photos.description: Historic 1932 photograph of iconic Mexican painter Frida Kahlo taken by her father, photographer Guillermo Kahlo, in Coyoacán. Highlights her resolute gaze, indigenous Tehuana attire, and deep connection to Mexican folk identity.

photos.title: The Valley of Mexico from the Hill of Santa Isabel — José María Velasco, 1877, Mexico
photos.description: Monumental 1877 landscape canvas by Mexican master José María Velasco. Captures the sweeping geological expanse of the Valley of Mexico with the Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl volcanoes rising beneath majestic cumulus clouds.

photos.title: Murals of Bonampak (Musicians and Procession) — Maya Civilization, c. 790 AD, Chiapas, Mexico
photos.description: Ancient Maya fresco in Structure 1 of the ruins of Bonampak in Chiapas, Mexico (c. 790 AD). Shows Mayan royal musicians playing turtle carapaces, rattles, and long wooden trumpets in a vibrant ceremony painted with brilliant Maya Blue.

photos.title: The Raven and the First Men — Bill Reid, 1980, Haida Nation / Vancouver, Canada
photos.description: Monumental yellow cedar carving by master Haida artist Bill Reid (1980) at the Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver. Illustrates the Haida creation myth of Raven coaxing the first human beings out of a giant clamshell on the shores of Haida Gwaii.

photos.title: Moche Portrait Vessel of a Ruler — Moche Culture, c. 450 AD, Larco Museum, Lima, Peru
photos.description: Finely modeled stirrup-spout ceramic vessel of the Moche culture of ancient Peru (c. 450 AD). Features an individualized realistic human portrait of an elite Moche dignitary with ornate headdress, ear spools, and painted facial markings.

photos.title: Queen Nefertari Playing Senet — Tomb of Nefertari, c. 1255 BC, Valley of the Queens, Luxor, Egypt
photos.description: Vibrant 19th Dynasty Egyptian wall painting from the Tomb of Queen Nefertari (QV66) in the Valley of the Queens (c. 1255 BC). The Great Royal Wife of Ramesses II plays the game of senet to pass safely into the afterlife, wearing a pleated linen gown and vulture headdress.

photos.title: Nebamun Hunting in the Marshes — Tomb of Nebamun, c. 1350 BC, Thebes / Luxor, Egypt
photos.description: Famous 18th Dynasty Egyptian fresco fragment from the tomb-chapel of scribe Nebamun at Thebes (c. 1350 BC). Nebamun stands on a reed skiff in the papyrus marsh hunting birds with a throwstick, surrounded by lotus flowers and a hunting cat.

photos.title: Saint George and the Dragon — Ethiopian Diptych Icon, 17th c., Tigray, Ethiopia
photos.description: 17th-century Ethiopian Christian diptych icon from the Tigray highlands, painted in tempera on wood. Depicts Saint George mounted on a white charger slaying the dragon, executed in the distinctive vibrant, graphic Gondarine style.

photos.title: Olowe of Ise Carved Veranda Post — Yoruba Kingdom, c. 1910, Ekiti / Ikere, Nigeria
photos.description: Magnificent architectural veranda post carved from a single trunk of wood by master Yoruba sculptor Olowe of Ise (c. 1910) for the royal palace of Ikere. Depicts an equestrian warrior king atop a horse with extraordinary vertical dynamism.

photos.title: Earth's Creation — Emily Kame Kngwarreye, 1994, Utopia, Northern Territory, Australia
photos.description: Monumental 1994 masterpiece by senior Aboriginal Australian artist Emily Kame Kngwarreye. Executed in swirling dots and sweeps of synthetic polymer paint, depicting Alhalkere after the monsoonal rains in the Australian Central Desert.

photos.title: Carved Canoe Prow (Tauihu) — Māori Whakairo Wood Carving, 18th c., Aotearoa / New Zealand
photos.description: 18th-century Māori war canoe prow (tauihu) carved from native tōtara wood with pounamu jade chisels. Features intricate spirals (pitau) and stylized ancestral guardian figures (manaia) with iridescent pāua shell eyes, personifying ocean navigation power.

photos.title: Portrait of a Beauty (Miindo) — Shin Yun-bok (Hyewon), c. 1805, Joseon Dynasty, Seoul, Korea
photos.description: Masterpiece genre painting by Joseon Dynasty master Shin Yun-bok (Hyewon, c. 1805). Portrays an elegant gisaeng with an elaborate braided hairstyle (eonjeun meori) touching the norigae ornament of her hanbok, revered as the epitome of Korean feminine beauty.

photos.title: Wang Xizhi Watching Geese — Qian Xuan, c. 1295, Yuan Dynasty, Metropolitan Museum of Art
photos.description: Yuan Dynasty handscroll by Qian Xuan (c. 1295), one of the Eight Talents of Wuxing. Depicts the legendary 4th-century Calligrapher Sage Wang Xizhi leaning from a pavilion watching swimming geese, whose fluid neck movements inspired cursive calligraphy.
